_comment: Hand-established ground truth for tools/catalog-recall.js. NOT generated.
Each entry was built by reading the lab's README for what it claims to implement and
then confirming each claim against the lab's own source, in whatever language that
source is written in. It is deliberately NOT built from the scanner's output, which
is the thing being measured: ground truth derived from the tool under test measures
nothing at all.
`implements` is the in-vocabulary truth: algorithms the lab computes that a term in
catalog-vocab.js could match. Recall is measured against this and nothing else.
`outOfVocabulary` is the lab's other implemented algorithms, for which no term
exists. These are NOT recall failures - the scanner cannot be blamed for missing a
term nobody wrote - but they are the vocabulary's coverage debt, counted separately
so the two failures never get averaged into one comfortable number.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE WHOLE FLEET, AND CANNOT BE GENERATED INTO ONE.
Every entry costs a hand read: the lab's README for what it claims, then its own
source, in whatever language, to confirm each claim. That is the one thing that
cannot be automated here, because the only tool that could do it is the tool being
measured - ground truth derived from catalog-evidence would report 100% and mean
nothing. 208 labs of that reading is a hand audit, not a generated fixture, and a
fixture assembled quickly to cover more ground is the exact failure `grown` names.
'Every lab with a hand-rolled implementation' is also not a set this fixture can
address, and the reason is worth keeping: strata come from the scanner's own
IMPLEMENTATION_SHAPES, which are first-match-wins, so one crypto.subtle call makes
a lab 'WebCrypto' however much it hand-rolls. crypto-lab-air-stream hand-rolls both
SNOW 3G and ZUC and is classified WebCrypto for a single AES block call. The
'hand-rolled' stratum is therefore labs that use NO library at all, not labs
containing a hand-rolled implementation - a distinction that decides which labs a
sampling rule can even reach.
method: Round 1 (12 labs, 2026-09-24) was stratified by implementation style and taken at fixed intervals through each stratum in sorted order. That method is NOT stable under growth - changing the count reshuffles every pick, so a larger fixture would not contain the smaller one and the two could not be compared. Round 2 (to 20 labs, 2026-09-24) therefore orders each stratum by sha1(slug) and takes the first N not already present, which makes every future extension a superset. Targets over-weight the small strata on purpose: WebCrypto 6 (of 92), @noble 5 (46), hand-rolled 5 (44), UNKNOWN 3 (14), partially-unread 1 (9). The two NOT-SCANNED labs are excluded by construction - there is no finding to measure. Strata come from the scanner's OWN implementation classification, which is a limitation worth stating: a lab it badly misreads could be mis-stratified. Round 3 (to 21 labs, 2026-09-29) adds one lab OUT OF sha1 order and says so in the entry: crypto-lab-air-stream is the regression witness for the vocabulary class, not a sample pick, and the sha1 ordering of every other stratum is untouched so the superset property still holds for future growth.

crypto-lab-aegis-gate.how: aegis256Encrypt/Decrypt and aesRound/SBOX in src/; benchmarkAesGcm calls WebCrypto AES-GCM.

crypto-lab-hpke-envelope.how: src/hpke/{dhkem,aead,context}.ts compose DHKEM(X25519,HKDF-SHA256) with AES-128-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305; both AEADs present in src/hpke/aead.ts.

crypto-lab-pq-families.how: src/crypto.ts exports lamportKeygen and digestMessage; the rest of the lab is a landscape map, not implementations.

crypto-lab-accumulator.how: RSA-group accumulate/absenceProof over an RSA modulus; SHA-256 via @noble/hashes/sha256. Judgement recorded: it computes in an RSA group and implements no RSA encryption or signature.

crypto-lab-frozen-heart.how: src/schnorr/group.ts imports RistrettoPoint and ed25519 from @noble/curves; fiatshamir.ts computes the challenge; sha512 from @noble/hashes.

crypto-lab-pake-gate.how: src/pake/factories.ts builds SRP-6a, J-PAKE, CPace and Dragonfly by hand; src/pake/hashes.ts derives with HKDF. Three of the four PAKEs have no vocabulary term.

crypto-lab-blind-hello.how: buildClientHello/decodeClientHelloInner construct and parse real TLS 1.3 ClientHello structures with ECH extensions.

crypto-lab-fte.how: aesCtrEncrypt/aesCtrDecrypt in src/; the regex-ranked DFA machinery is the lab's own subject and has no term.

crypto-lab-ntru-classic.how: generateKeyPair/encrypt/decrypt over the 1996 HPS parameter set, with centerMod and ternary polynomial arithmetic.

crypto-lab-biham-lens.how: Differential cryptanalysis against a toy SPN built for the lesson. No standard algorithm is computed, so UNKNOWN is the correct finding rather than a miss.

crypto-lab-hqc-timing-break.how: runAttack/llr simulate a cache-timing oracle; the README states a repetition code stands in for HQC's Reed-Muller inner code. Implements neither HQC nor Reed-Muller, so UNKNOWN is correct.

crypto-lab-context-ward.how: src/primitives.ts exports sha256, hmacSha256, hkdfSha256, ed25519Sign/Verify. One Python file in the repo is not read by the scanner.

crypto-lab-harvest-vault.how: dhKeyPair/dhShared/modPow implement finite-field DH. kemKeyGen/kemEncapsulate/kemDecapsulate with polyMul, polyAdd and samplePolyNoise implement a polynomial-ring LWE KEM. JUDGEMENT RECORDED: the ring-LWE KEM is genuinely computed but the source never writes the name anywhere, so no name-based scanner can find it.

crypto-lab-commit-gate.how: README states SHA-256 hash commitments and Pedersen commitments over P-256; commitPedersen and the P-256 group operations are in src/.

crypto-lab-stark-tower.how: friFromTrace and friDemo run the FRI low-degree test, buildMerkle/openMerkle the commitment, and src/merkle.ts hashes with SHA-256.

crypto-lab-kem-trap.how: imports @noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js plus hkdf, hmac, sha2 and sha3 from @noble/hashes; encapsulate/decapsulate and deriveSessionKey call them.

crypto-lab-ibe-gate.how: imports @noble/curves/bls12-381.js and @noble/hashes/sha2.js; extract/encrypt/decrypt implement BasicIdent over the pairing. NOTE: it uses the BLS12-381 CURVE and implements no BLS signature scheme - the two are separate terms and the card should not be read as claiming the latter.

crypto-lab-ggh-trapdoor.how: big-integer lattice basis arithmetic implementing the Goldreich-Goldwasser-Halevi trapdoor: same lattice, a short basis that decrypts and a long one that does not.

crypto-lab-blind-oracle.how: imports the 'tfhe' package (Zama TFHE-rs WASM build); encryptValue/decryptResult/computeAdd operate on FheUint8 ciphertexts.

crypto-lab-matsui-line.how: linear cryptanalysis against the same toy 4-round SPN that crypto-lab-biham-lens attacks with differentials. DES is discussed as the historical target and never implemented, so UNKNOWN is the correct finding.

crypto-lab-air-stream.addedOutOfOrder: 2026-09-29, as a REGRESSION WITNESS rather than a sample pick. This is the lab whose missing ZUC term exposed the vocabulary class as open outside the sample, so it belongs in the measurement that claims the class is closed. It is declared here rather than slipped in, because the sha1(slug) growth rule exists so every later fixture is a superset of every earlier one, and a silent out-of-order pick would break that property without anyone noticing.
crypto-lab-air-stream.how: Ground truth read from README 'What It Is' (128-EEA1/SNOW 3G, 128-EEA2/AES-CTR, 128-EEA3/ZUC) and confirmed in source. SNOW 3G hand-rolled in src/snow/snow3g.ts (LFSR/FSM clock, SNOW_SQ S-box in constants.ts, generateSnowEea1Keystream:227, encryptSnowEea1:250). ZUC hand-rolled in src/zuc/zuc.ts (GF(2^31-1) add31/rotate31:23-30, generateZucEea3Keystream:177, encryptZucEea3:199; ZUC_D/S0/S1 in constants.ts), KAT from the GSMA EEA3/EIA3 implementors' data and cross-checked against @li0ard/zuc. AES via crypto.subtle in src/aes/eea2.ts:19-27. AES-CTR is implemented in that same file - buildEea2Counter:31 plus the keystream XOR - and the string 'CTR' appears nowhere in it, so it is an unnamed-implementation miss by construction. NOT listed: AES-CBC, which the scanner credits from the WebCrypto algorithm name at eea2.ts:19; that call is a single-block primitive with a zero IV used to build CTR, and the lab implements no chaining. The fixture measures recall over a verified subset, so leaving it out records it as out of scope rather than as a false positive - precision is measured the other way round, by reading anchors.

grown: Grown as the work goes, not when a threshold is in reach. A fixture assembled to clear a gate measures the gate.
